newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil May 8-June 8 Fipe inflation at 0.82 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil May 8-June 8 Fipe inflation at 0.82 pct.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.82 percent between May 8 and June 8, up from 0.55 percent in the previous four week period, a Fipe official said.
Juarez Rizzieri, president of the Fipe institute, said a 4.91 percent rise in clothing prices and a recent hike in telephone and electricity rates contributed to higher inflation in the period.
Rizzieri said higher telephone rates had an impact of 0.31 percent on the Fipe index, while electricity rates had an impact of 0.27 percent.
He also said he expects inflation for the whole month of June to be around 1.0 percent.
The Fipe president released the following breakdown of Fipe's weighted inflation index for May 8 through June 8:
- Food: -0.70 pct drop in the period
- Housing: 2.32 pct rise in the period
- Transportation: -0.02 pct drop in the period
- Personal expenses: -0.33 pct drop in the period
- Clothing: 4.91 pct rise in the period
- Health care: 1.24 pct rise in the period
- Education: -0.02 pct drop in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures weekly.
